messages:
sam: FYI - noticed a perf regression in prod inference after the kernel-selector tweak rolled out this morning. 99th latency for short sequences jumped ~18%. I captured an nsys trace + perf flame. nsys timeline shows more CPU on the tokenizer and our scheduler spin; nvprof indicates a fallback to the generic convolution kernel more often. trace: https://perf.company/nsys/1768453210 and flame: https://perf.company/flames/1768453210

maia: When did that rollout happen? which config changed? :eyes:

sam: Deploy was at 1768450000, config key was kernel_selector.enable_fallback_score=true (small tweak to prefer lower-cost kernels). Repro script: `./tools/run_small_seq_load.sh --qps 150 --seq 32`

cheng: Quick paste of `perf script` stackcollapse excerpt I grabbed from the run (collapsed stacks):
```
runtime.py;batcher.py;tokenizer.py  1187
batcher.py;scheduler.c;spin_wait  923
tokenizer.c;utf8_scan  600
kernel_selector.c;select_kernel  450
```
Looks like more time is on tokenizer+spin_wait vs previous runs where GPU kernels dominated.

ravi: Hm. My theory: the selector prefers a faster kernel variant but that variant expects the KV cache to be warm; when it isn't we end up doing extra CPU tokenization + cache warmups and then falling back, adding cycles. So the heuristic increases churn for short, bursty requests.

maia: If that's true, a short-term mitigation is to revert the fallback heuristic for sequences < 64 tokens. Can we flip a flag? Also we should add a perf test simulating cold KV cache bursts.

sam: I'll flip the flag on prod staging gates now and re-run the workload. Creating a rollback: `rtnctl feature toggle kernel_selector.enable_fallback_score --off --env prod`

perf-bot: Benchmark job created: https://ci.company/bench/1768453210-rollback-check. nsys and perf artifacts will be posted once finished.

cheng: After the toggle rollback, I re-ran the same trace. 99th is back within 2% of baseline. New collapsed stacks show the kernel selection path no longer in the hot path; GPU kernel time increased again.

ravi: Sounds like confirmed. Action items: 1) revert the selector change until we add a cache-warmth check 2) add unit/regression perf test for short-seq cold-cache bursts 3) tighten threshold and add metric to track fallback frequency. I'll open the PR for the selector guard.

maia: Please also add a dashboard alarm for fallback-rate and a synthetic job that runs the small-seq pattern every 5m so we detect recurrence.

sam: Will do. I'll draft a short postmortem and link traces/artifacts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Artifacts uploaded: nsys: https://perf.company/nsys/1768453210/after_rollback, flame: https://perf.company/flames/1768453210/after_rollback
